newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Sell India Grasim - Peregrine.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Sell India Grasim - Peregrine.

text.p: Peregrine Capital India said it recommended investors to sell Grasim Industries' domestic stocks and global depositary receipts (GDRs) listed overseas because of poor short-term growth prospects.

"While we believe that the long-term fundamentals are strong, the stock will continue to underperform the Sensex (30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index) in the medium term," the securities firm said in a report. "We recommend a SELL."
It said the diversified firm's earnings growth this year would see a fall due to dimmed prospects for viscose staple fibre (VSF) and cement, two of its vital products.

"We expect Grasim's EPS to drop by 10 percent in FY97 (financial year ending March 31, 1997) and then grow by a 7 percent CAGR (compounded annual growth rate) to FY99 -- considerably lower than the 17 percent EPS growth for the Sensex," analysts V. Ramanan and B. Sashikanth said.
Though the firm has postponed a $125 million GDR issue due to sluggish market conditions, the two analysts saw little chance of this pushing the stock.
"Given the lacklustre prospects for the local stock, we expect the GDR to move with the local stock. We recommend a SELL on GDR," the report said.
The analysts said that a re-rating would depend on recovery in polyester staple fibre (PSF).
"Only a sharp recovery in international PSF prices will reverse the downward trend in the VSF industry," the report said. "We do not see this happening in the next six months."
PSF prices were below VSF prices for the first time in two decades, the analysts said.
Volume growth in the cement division was expected to go up 33 percent but surpluses in Grasim's markets and 15 percent increase in input costs will eat into margins, they said.
